Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@novahealth.com>, security_team@novahealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Subprocessor inventory & evidence for Nova Health SIG submission

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Our InfoSec team is collecting SIG/CAIQ materials for a planned vendor review next week and asked if Redwood can provide: 1) a current subprocessor inventory with roles and data-access levels; 2) redacted SOC 2 Type II evidence or a summary; and 3) a short KMS/key management access matrix (who has admin access, where keys are stored).

Specifically, they want a CSV we can ingest into our SIG intake tool, and any supporting PDFs we can attach. Can you confirm what you can share and the expected delivery timeline? If there are any portal links or gated reports, a short note on how we can access them (SAML/one-time link) would be helpful.

Our timeline is tight — ideally by COB Tuesday, 2026-12-01. If you need an NDA or redaction plan, let me know.

Appreciate it,

Emma Ross
Senior Security Analyst
Nova Health Systems
emma.ross@novahealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0127
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory & evidence for Nova Health SIG submission

Emma,

Thanks — we can provide a CSV with the subprocessor catalog plus a redacted SOC2 summary and a KMS access matrix. A couple quick notes:

- SOC 2 Type II full report is shared via a protected portal (SAML). We can either add a Nova Health account if you want persistent access, or provide a time-limited PDF export with standard redactions.
- The subprocessor CSV we generate includes: vendor name, function (e.g., hosting, monitoring), data types processed, legal basis, region, and access level (admin/limited/none).
- KMS matrix will show role-level access (Redwood secure operations, SRE, customer-managed options).

We do have a standard evidence delivery process for procurement/security teams — small paperwork (NDA + DPA acknowledgement) to permit delivery of sensitive artefacts. If Nova Health already has an NDA on file from procurement, forward the Doc ID and we'll skip duplication. Otherwise, we can redact account-identifying event logs and deliver the artifacts.

Target: I will coordinate with Marcus to produce the CSV and redacted artifacts and aim to deliver by Tue 2026-12-01 EOD PST. Please confirm whether you prefer portal access or a zipped package via our secure transfer.

Best,

Priya Natarajan
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
+1 (646) 555-0199

Attaching the initial pack per Priya's note — see the README for delivery notes. We generated the CSV export and included a short SOC2 summary (redacted for customer tokens and request-specific logs). The SOC2 summary contains control descriptions and scope; the full Type II report is available through our compliance portal (link below) and requires a one-time SAML invitation (I can add your group if you confirm the email list).

Attachments in this email:
- 20261130_Redwood_Subprocessors.csv (CSV)
- SOC2_summary_redacted_2026.pdf (PDF)

Delivery notes:
- The CSV includes a column 'access_level' with values {admin, privileged, restricted, none}. 'Privileged' indicates ability to access customer runtime artifacts for troubleshooting under L0 playbook.
- For hosting subprocessor entries, region reflects contracted data residency; some infra providers are multi-region — we noted primary region column.
- If you need a format change for the SIG tool (Semgrep/ScoreCard ingest), tell us which fields map and we can re-export.

Portal link (SOC2 full report): https://redwood.sharepoint.com/soc2/REDWOOD_SOC2_2026_T2

Priya / Marcus,

Thanks — we received the CSV and the PDFs. Quick follow-ups from the InfoSec review:

1) Can you provide a short statement (one paragraph) for each hosting/infra subprocessor indicating whether they have access to unencrypted customer data in production? A simple yes/no plus brief justification is sufficient.
2) For KMS, can you indicate whether any Redwood personnel have persistent key admin roles (not on-call emergency access) and whether HSMs are customer-sequestered for private deployments?

We will ingest the CSV into our SIG tool today; the team will follow up if mapping issues appear. If possible, send the one-paragraph answers by EOD Wednesday (2026-12-02) so we can finish internal sign-off Thursday.

Also — thanks for the portal link. For speed, the time-limited PDF worked fine. If you provision SAML access later that would be helpful for ongoing audits.

Regards,
